articles.title_original: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
articles.title_zh: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
facts_zh:
Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
- Published
Prosecutors in the United States have accused Venezuela's former leader Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, of conspiracy to commit torture.
The fresh charges against the couple were made public on Thursday and are in addition to the drug-trafficking and weapons charges already brought against them, which they have denied.

Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, have been in custody since January in a detention centre in Brooklyn, where they were taken after US forces seized them in a pre-dawn raid on their compound in the Venezuelan capital, Caracas.

all_titles.en: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

articles.title_original: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
articles.title_zh: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
facts_zh:
Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain
- Published
Most diplomats will leave the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, Israel says, but the UK insists the building "will not be closing" and will operate as a "UK Mission".

"We did not want it to come to this," Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar wrote on social media, as he said 20 diplomats and the consul general would leave while a task force of seven could remain in the building "with a very limited scope of activity".
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband responded that some staff had been "temporarily withdrawn" for security reasons, and stressed the mission would continue "our work with the Palestinian people".

all_titles.en: Most UK diplomats to leave East Jerusalem consulate, Israel says, as Miliband says 'vital services' to remain

articles.title_original: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
articles.title_zh: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
facts_zh:
Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
- Published
Christa Pike is "up and walking" though mentally "foggy" while in hospital after last week's botched attempt to execute her in the US state of Tennessee, her legal team says.
Pike, 50, who was sentenced to death after murdering Colleen Slemmer with her then-boyfriend in 1995, survived two lethal injections on 30 September.
Experts described it as unprecedented.

all_titles.en: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC

articles.title_original: Nicolás Maduro and his wife indicted for alleged torture of US citizens
articles.title_zh: Nicolás Maduro and his wife indicted for alleged torture of US citizens
facts_zh: Ousted Venezuelan president and Cilia Flores have been in jail in New York since early January The deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, have been indicted for alleged conspiracy to commit torture, according to Manhattan federal court papers unsealed on Thursday.
The superseding indictment was unsealed shortly before Flores appeared at court in her ongoing push for pre-trial release – which was denied by Judge Alvin Hellerstein.
Maduro and Flores have been held in a New York City jail since early January.

all_titles.en: Nicolás Maduro and his wife indicted for alleged torture of US citizens

articles.title_original: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'
articles.title_zh: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'
facts_zh:
Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'
- Published
Italy's parliament has approved fiercely contested changes to the country's electoral system championed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni ahead of elections due next year.
Lawmakers voted 227 to 164 in favour of moving to a fully proportional system, which Meloni has argued will boost the chance of clear winners and more stable government.

Opposition parties say her right-wing coalition has designed the proposals to improve its chance of retaining power and, in a heated debate on Thursday, accused it of pushing through the "fraudulent" reform to flout democracy.

all_titles.en: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'

articles.title_original: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
articles.title_zh: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
facts_zh:
Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
- Published
A tanker has been struck by "multiple projectiles" north of Qatar in the Gulf, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency.
The incident - a rare attack deep inside the Gulf - happened 51 nautical miles (94km) from Madinat al-Shamal with casualties reported, the UKMTO said.
Maritime intelligence firm Vanguard identified the vessel as the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged oil and chemical tanker Acers.

all_titles.en: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says

articles.title_original: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
articles.title_zh: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
facts_zh:
Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
- Published
Police in central Chile have airlifted several residents to safety after rising floodwaters left them trapped in their homes.
Recent torrential rains caused the Mapocho river to burst its banks, flooding large parts of the city of Talagante, 35km (22 miles) south-west of the capital, Santiago.
Santiago has seen 74mm of rainfall in the first seven days of this month, making it the rainiest October for the area in 76 years, meteorologists have said.

all_titles.en: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile

articles.title_original: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
articles.title_zh: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
facts_zh:
Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
- Published
An elderly woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis and a political row that triggered early elections has died, according to Madrid's tenants union.
Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years on 23 September after she was unable to afford steep rent increases.
The company that owned the flat later offered to allow her to return at a lower rate - but she was unable to sign an agreement as she had been admitted to hospital.

all_titles.en: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
